claims.text: Elemental Cr coating protects zirconium-alloy cladding in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of conventional Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
A 100–200 nm TiN interlayer should be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating.
The deposited TiN interlayer will be dense.
The TiN interlayer acts as a physical diffusion barrier between Cr and Zr.
TiN is chemically inert under the proposed service conditions.
TiN is thermally stable under the proposed service conditions.
The TiN barrier inhibits Cr–Zr interfacial atomic transport during high-temperature exposure.
The TiN interlayer allows the outer Cr coating to continue providing oxidation protection.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the coating's structural and chemical integrity.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control, TiN-interlayered samples will show reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control, TiN-interlayered samples will retain greater coating integrity, including less degradation or blistering.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control, TiN-interlayered samples will have comparable or improved oxidation resistance.
The proposed intervention is applicable at approximately 300°C in high-pressure subcritical water for hundreds to thousands of hours.
The proposed intervention is applicable in high-temperature steam at up to approximately 1200°C for about 30 minutes.
The TiN interlayer's stability under prolonged neutron irradiation is uncertain.
Unforeseen chemical interactions may occur between TiN and adjacent Cr or Zr under extreme conditions.
